pr_title: docs: fix routing code to use `navigate`
pr_body:
Previously, the example in the `router` guide was not
preserving the query params after logging in.

This commit fixes this by using `navigate` instead of
using `navigateByUrl`, which ignores any properties in
the `NavigationExtras` that would change the provided URL.

Fixes #34917

issue_context.title: Potential bug in the routing example stackblitz program
issue_context.body:
# 📚 Docs or angular.io bug report ### Description The example presented in https://angular.io/generated/live-examples/router/stackblitz.html (live example) does not exhibit the behaviour claimed in the documentation at https://angular.io/guide/router#query-parameters-and-fragments. Namely, this: > Now, you can click on the Admin button, which takes you to the Login page with the provided queryParamMap and fragment. After you click the login button, notice that you have been redirected to the Admin Dashboard page with the query parameters and fragment still intact in the address bar. The query parameter and the fragment both get lost when you are forwarded to the "admin" page by the login button. You can see that the "Admin" page displays `Null` both for `Session ID` and for `Token`, as they are also absent in the address bar. The cause seems to be the `navigateByUrl()` call in `auth/login/login.component.ts` at line 40. This is what the official doc says for this function referring to its `extras` parameter: > NavigationExtras | An object containing properties that modify the navigation strategy. The function ignores any properties in the NavigationExtras that would change the provided URL. So if you replace line 40 ``` this.router.navigateByUrl(redirect, navigationExtras); ``` with ``` this.router.navigate([this.authService.redirectUrl], navigationExtras); ``` the app behaviour is then consistent with the expected description in the angular write-up. While `navigate()` is normally doing a relative navigation, in the absence of a "start" (`relativeTo`) position it will do the absolute navigation, but without the adverse effect of `navigateByUrl()`. Maybe not the most optimal solution though But notice that if this solution is adopted, the `UrlTree` `redirect` variable is then not necessary Also the Angular Doc write–up has to be updated as well to whatever solution is adopted ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction ### What's the affected URL?** https://angular.io/generated/live-examples/router/stackblitz.html and the documentation at https://angular.io/guide/router#query-parameters-and-fragments ### Reproduction Steps** Navigate to https://angular.io/generated/live-examples/router/stackblitz.html, then to `Admin` tab and click the `Login` button. You will see both `Session ID` and `Token` being `None` ### Expected vs Actual Behavior** `Session ID` should be `123456789`, and `Token` should be `anchor`, and not `None` Otherwise how are they persistent? ## 📷Screenshot ## 🔥 Exception or Error
## 🌍 Your Environment ### Browser info ### Anything else relevant?
comments:
Thx for reporting this, @pasha-bolokhov, and for suggesting a solution.
Indeed the docs of [Router#navigateByUrl()][1] mention:

> The function ignores any properties in the `NavigationExtras` that would change the provided URL.

So, apparently, query params and fragment options are ignored.
The possible fix is to switch to the [Router#navigate()][2] method (as @pasha-bolokhov suggested). I.e. we need to change the code in [examples/router/src/app/auth/login/login.component.1.ts][3] and [examples/router/src/app/auth/login/login.component.ts][4] to something like:

```diff
         // Get the redirect URL from our auth service
         // If no redirect has been set, use the default
-        let redirect = this.authService.redirectUrl ? this.router.parseUrl(this.authService.redirectUrl) : '/admin';
+        const redirectUrl = this.authService.redirectUrl || '/admin';

         ...

         // Redirect the user
-        this.router.navigateByUrl(redirect);
+        this.router.navigate([redirectUrl]);                    // For `login.component.1.ts`.
+        this.router.navigate([redirectUrl], navigationExtras);  // For `login.component.ts`.
```

We should also add a test in [examples/router/e2e/src/app.e2e-spec.ts][5] to verify that this scenario works as described in the guide.

[1]: https://v9.angular.io/api/router/Router#navigateByUrl
[2]: https://next.angular.io/api/router/Router#navigate
[3]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/128d4ac8a/aio/content/examples/router/src/app/auth/login/login.component.1.ts#L28-L33
[4]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/128d4ac8a/aio/content/examples/router/src/app/auth/login/login.component.ts#L29-L43
[5]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/128d4ac8a/aio/content/examples/router/e2e/src/app.e2e-spec.ts
@gkalpak As discussed offline, I will take this issue.

Closing this since #35176 merged. @pasha-bolokhov, if you still have questions, feel free to continue commenting here or to reopen if the issue isn't resolved for you. Thank you for pointing this out and thanks to @sonukapoor for resolving!

Is this information reflected in the user documentation that accompanies the example? I think that's important.

Having code comments is great, but it's better when it supports/compliments the content in the user doc. There are a number of reasons for this, but probably the most important one is the simplest: We never know what users are going to read, or when, or even where! (Makes writing documentation interesting...)
